field_rule: First check SCALE and the BASAL BUNCH: Lindheimer muhly forms a large coarse, densely tufted fountain often around 0.8–1.5 m tall, with tall relatively contracted, densely flowered panicles. field_rule: Knotgrass combines wet-ground creeping stolons with usually paired (rarely three) unilateral flowering racemes. Bahia grass can produce two racemes but differs in low turf/rhizome architecture and spikelet structure. Thin paspalum may form just one or a few flowering branches but has different leafy habit and varietal hair traits; Florida paspalum forms robust upright bunches and bigger oval spikelets.

field_rule: Actual archived Bob Harms whole flowering-specimen panel 1 shows several attached leafy shoots and panicles; panel 2 displays the entire dense short-branched seedhead; panel 3 magnifies overlapping glumes. A contracted ovoid to cylindrical head is a first clue (FNA 0.5–8 cm long, often 0.8–2 cm wide), but several introduced Phalaris look similar. The one- vs two-STERILE-LEMMA difference cannot be determined from head silhouette alone.
